- Suggestion: Find an eligible Open thread in the fixture items and explicitly select its platform and visible list row before checking the summary marker.

glm.feedback:
- Category: spec
- Severity: medium
- File: integration-tests/e2e-webui/src/baseline/checks-board.ts:155 (commentCount)
- Finding: AC 1 says "comment-count text counts visible elements only", but only the second half of the disjunction was fixed. `leafCount(b.page, re) >= 2` still counts hidden elements, so if the phone picker's hidden `<option>`s repeat "N comments" text (exactly the bug class this iterate fixes), the check passes via `leafCount` even though neither visible place shows the count — a false pass the harness was supposed to eliminate.
- Suggestion: Apply the visible filter to the `leafCount` side too (e.g. pass a visible-only variant of the leaf counter, or drop the `leafCount` half and count with `visibleText` alone), or make the assertion require both the row and the header to be visible matches.

- Category: edge-case
- Severity: low
- File: integration-tests/e2e-webui/src/baseline/checks-static.ts:22-24 (checkStoreOnly)
- Finding: The mandated-text carve-out is applied to *every* file's code text, so any file that happens to contain the sentence "this lesson is already in lessons.md" gets that occurrence removed before the FILE_NAME scan. If a real file access elsewhere is documented in a comment that quotes the full sentence, the `lessons.md` mention inside it is also masked. The unit test only probes the sentence alone, not a masked access sharing a line with it.
- Suggestion: Narrow the carve-out (e.g. only strip occurrences that are not part of a `FILE_NAME` match context), or accept and document the residual risk; at minimum add a unit case with the sentence and a real access in the same file.

- Category: bug
- Severity: low
- File: integration-tests/e2e-webui/src/baseline/checks-board.ts:170-171 (copyAndOpen)
- Finding: `copy.elementHandle()` is grabbed before the click; if the app re-renders the button on click (React-style replace rather than mutate), the stale handle's `innerText` resolves on a detached node and returns `""` via the catch, making the "Copied" check fail against a correct app. The old role lookup would at least have re-queried. This is the same fragility the iterate set out to remove, just inverted.
- Suggestion: After the click, re-query the button by a stable attribute (e.g. within the thread view's action bar) rather than freezing an `elementHandle`, or verify via a locator scoped to the container that keeps identity across re-renders.

- Category: test
- Severity: low
- File: integration-tests/e2e-webui/tests/unit/baseline-harness-fixes.spec.ts:17-19
- Finding: The "no key" fallback branch of `listRow` is only exercised on a page with exactly one row, so it doesn't prove the fallback avoids the hidden `<option>` when multiple `[data-k]` rows exist or the fallback itself mis-selects. A broken fallback (e.g. text lookup without the row constraint) would still pass this test as written, since the test page has no hidden-option ambiguity in the fallback path.
- Suggestion: Add a hidden `<option>` with a *different* thread's title and two rows, then assert the fallback clicks the row whose title matches, not any element containing the text.

- Category: edge-case
- Severity: low
- File: integration-tests/e2e-webui/src/baseline/board-ui.ts:60-63 (listRow)
- Finding: The CSS attribute selector escapes only `"` and `\` in the key. Thread keys are platform slugs, so this is fine in practice, but if `str(item.key)` were empty the code silently falls back to the text path even when `item.key` was expected — combined with `filter({ hasText: rowTitle })` truncating at 60 chars, two threads whose titles share the first 60 characters would make the fallback open the wrong thread (a real hazard for long HN titles that repeat).
- Suggestion: In the fallback, additionally assert the clicked row's `data-k` equals the expected key after click (or match on the full title), to guard against the 60-char truncation ambiguity.

Positive notes: B17's `plain` join, B31's package-wide host scan with the per-file outside check preserved, the recheck project wiring (non-zero exit on hard reds, `expect(b.some(...))` guard against an empty run), and the tour fixes (case-insensitive marker, platform re-pick for the Expired filter) all match the acceptance criteria and are covered by real-behavior unit tests, not smoke tests.

Overall: the harness fixes are correct in direction and mostly well-tested, but AC 1 is only half-applied to the comment-count check (hidden elements can still produce a false pass), so ship-with-fixes.

SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
